title: Uptime partner workshop agenda and mini-pilot plan - Nov 2026
body:
Purpose:
Run a focused cross-functional half-day workshop with partner product and infra teams to align on critical-path uptime objectives, then launch a 4-week mini-pilot that validates an operational pattern for SLO activation and incident coordination. The output should be: a refined SLO success criterion, a lightweight escalation & routing protocol, and a concrete pilot backlog with owners and measurable signals.

Context and rationale:
- We are seeing increasing customer reliance on low-latency hosted endpoints and Dedicated pools; recent incidents (see JIRA-SRE-7890) highlighted unclear ownership for transient GPU pool degradation and fallback routing behavior.
- This workshop is intended to create a repeatable, low-friction pattern teams can adopt to accelerate SLO adoption without heavy process overhead.
- Mini-pilot scope is deliberately small: 1 product route (customer-facing text-generation), the Dedicated serving pool for that route, and observability + escalation wiring.

Attendees (workshop):
- SRE: Priya Natarajan (facilitator), Ethan Walker (observability lead), Maya Chen (oncall/process)
- Product: Omar Haddad (product manager for TextGen), Lena Ruiz (PM partner)
- Infra/Runtime: Carlos Mendes (serving runtime lead), Sasha Kwon (capacity)
- Solutions Eng / CS: Mei Tan (customer success coverage for pilot customer)

Agenda (3.5 hours):
- 0:00–0:10 — Kickoff: goals, expected outputs, ground rules (Priya)
- 0:10–0:35 — Customer impact mapping: discuss worst-case user journeys for the selected route and map to business impact (Omar + Mei)
- 0:35–1:10 — Current state review: telemetry baseline (p50/p95 latency, error rate, time-of-day traffic), incident run-through of recent outage (Ethan)
- 1:10–1:35 — Define candidate SLOs: proposed objective, SLI definition (exact query types), measurement windows, error budget policy (all)
- 1:35–1:45 — Break
- 1:45–2:15 — Routing & fallback policy design: primary model, fallback variant selection, capacity tiering, cost tradeoffs (Carlos + Sasha)
- 2:15–2:45 — Escalation and playbook sketch: who gets paged, threshold triggers, automatic fallback vs human intervention (Maya)
- 2:45–3:10 — Mini-pilot plan and success criteria: timeline, acceptance metrics, stop/expand criteria (Priya + Omar)
- 3:10–3:20 — Quick risk heatmap and mitigation brainstorm (all)
- 3:20–3:30 — Action items and owners recap; commit to pilot start date

Workshop outputs (expected):
- Finalized SLO proposal for Route: /v1/generate-text (candidate SLO examples below).
- Simple SLI spec (promQL + synthetic check) and measurement doc reference.
- Escalation stub: page routing, 15-minute oncall window, second-level notification to runtime team.
- Pilot backlog of 8 tasks with owners and target completion dates.

Candidate SLOs (examples to finalize during workshop):
- Availability SLO: 99.9% of production requests to /v1/generate-text return HTTP 2xx within 350ms over a 30-day rolling window.
- Latency SLO (p95): p95 <= 450ms for inference responses for requests < 1024 tokens, 30-day rolling.
- Error budget policy: auto-failover to cheaper model variant if rolling 30-day availability drops below target AND current error budget consumed > 50%.

Mini-pilot plan (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep, 1 week before kick):
  - Instrument SLI: implement Prometheus metrics for request success/failure labeled by model-variant and pool (owner: Ethan, due: +5 days).
  - Baseline dashboards: create per-route p50/p95 latency, error rate, throughput (owner: Ethan, due: +7 days).
  - Synthetic check: deploy simple health-check runner that exercises representative prompts (owner: Omar + Mei, due: +7 days).
- Week 1 (pilot start):
  - Enable soft monitoring (alerts in read-only mode), runbook draft ready, and start capturing error budget burn rate (owner: Maya, due: pilot day).
  - Introduce customer-facing traffic to pilot bucket (10% of customers for the route) with traffic shaping (owner: Sasha, due: pilot day +1).
- Week 2 (validate routing & fallback):
  - Execute controlled fallback exercises: induce a constrained capacity condition in a staging-equivalent pool and observe automatic/manual failover (owner: Carlos, due: pilot day +10).
  - Review latency/backfill data; adjust thresholds.
- Week 3 (incident simulation & runbook rehearsal):
  - Run a 30-minute incident sim where oncall follows the playbook; capture timings and gaps (owner: Maya, due: pilot day +18).
  - Customer communication template test with CS (owner: Mei, due: pilot day +19).
- Week 4 (evaluation & decision):
  - Evaluate success metrics (SLO attainment, error budget consumption, operational overhead).
  - Decision gate: expand to 3 additional routes OR iterate on playbook (owner: Priya + Omar, decision due: pilot day +28).

Success metrics for pilot (quantitative + qualitative):
- Quantitative:
  - SLI measurement live and accurate (validated against synthetic checks).
  - SLO attainment > 98% for the pilot window OR documented error budget policy triggered correctly.
  - Mean time to detect (MTTD) < 3 minutes for paging conditions; mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) < 5 minutes.
- Qualitative:
  - Clear ownership identified for each failure mode (routing, model degradation, infra).
  - Playbook steps are actionable and took < 30 minutes to find and follow during sim.

Risks and mitigations (quick heatmap):
- Risk: Prometheus scrape cardinality increases due to per-model labels.
  - Mitigation: limit label cardinality by aggregating model variants into 3 categories during pilot (owner: Ethan).
- Risk: Fallback model produces lower-quality responses that cause customer complaints.
  - Mitigation: limit fallback to non-critical customers for pilot, add quality regression monitoring and immediate rollback path (owner: Omar + Mei).
- Risk: Oncall overload if alerts fire too frequently during traffic shaping.
  - Mitigation: tune alert thresholds conservatively initially and use paging escalation only for 15-minute sustained breaches (owner: Maya).

Action item template (to be filled at workshop close):
- [Task short title] — Owner — Due date — Acceptance criteria — Linked ticket
  - e.g., "Instrument SLI for /v1/generate-text" — Ethan — 2026-10-28 — PromQL returns correct success ratio for synthetic runner — JIRA-ENG-4521

Handoffs and operating notes:
- If pilot shows SLO regression, product PM (Omar) owns the customer communication draft; runtime (Carlos) owns immediate mitigation and rollback.
- For any telemetry gaps, SRE (Priya + Ethan) owns hotfix instrumentation and a postmortem of visibility issues.
- Documentation: add final SLI/SLO spec to Confluence under SRE > Uptime > pilots (owner: Priya).

Communications plan:
- Weekly pilot update email (short bullets) to: eng leadership, product leadership, CS pilot customer contact. Owner: Priya.
- Slack channel created: #pilot-uptime-textgen (owner: Omar).

Notes to self / facilitator reminders:
- Keep SLO definitions pragmatic and tied to easy-to-measure signals. Avoid multi-dimensional SLOs for the pilot.
- Emphasize recovery and fallbacks over zero-risk guarantees — we're validating process not perfect infra.
- Reserve 10 minutes at the end for a quick retro and assign next sync cadence (weekly during pilot).

Appendix: quick checklists
- Pre-workshop checklist:
  - Invite stakeholders + confirm schedule (Priya)
  - Share current dashboards and a 7-day incident summary (Ethan)
  - Provide a one-page SLO primer to attendees (Priya)
- Pilot launch checklist:
  - Synthetic runner green
  - Dashboards in read-only
  - Playbook draft accessible
  - Slack channel created and paging integrations verified

Planned dates and commitments:
- Workshop date (tentative): 2026-10-28 09:30–13:00 PT
- Pilot launch (target): 2026-11-02
- Pilot end / decision: 2026-11-30

Open questions for workshop:
- Which model variants are acceptable as fallback for production traffic? (Product + model owners decision)
- What is the lightweight reporting cadence product wants (daily summary vs weekly)?
- Should we include Dedicated pool autoscale rules as part of pilot or treat as separate follow-on?

Finish and next steps:
- Circulate this draft to collaborators for edits before workshop.
- Finalize invited attendee list and send pre-work (SLO primer + telemetry links) one week before workshop.

-- end of draft --
